question_text: A common misconception addressed in the course guide is that the system unit is the same as the:
explanation: The system unit has been confused by novices with the CPU, but the CPU (or processor) is just one component within the system unit, not the entire unit itself.

question_text: Read-Only Memory (ROM) chips are different from RAM chips in that ROM:
option_a: Loses its data the moment the PC is switched off
option_b: Has data written on it during manufacturing that remains even when the PC is switched off
option_c: Can only be used for sound processing
option_d: Requires a separate power source at all times
explanation: ROM chips have data written on them during manufacturing that tells the CPU what to do at startup; this data remains even when the PC is switched off, unlike RAM.

question_text: Cache memory, as described in the course guide, consists of:
option_a: Slow, cheap memory chips rarely used in modern PCs
option_b: Expensive and very fast memory chips that store data or instructions the CPU will look at next
option_c: A type of printer ink cartridge
explanation: Cache memory consists of expensive, very fast memory chips that store data or instructions the CPU is expected to need next, which can speed up the computer enormously.

question_text: The motherboard is described as being made of fiberglass because fiberglass:
option_b: Cannot conduct electricity, so each component is insulated from the others
explanation: Fiberglass cannot conduct electricity, so mounting components on it insulates each one from the others, with thin metal lines forming the electrical circuits.

question_text: Unlike RAM, the hard disk drive is described in the course guide as the computer's:
option_b: Main permanent storage unit, unaffected when the PC is turned off
explanation: The hard disk is the computer's main permanent storage unit; unlike RAM, information on it is not lost when the PC is turned off.

question_text: According to the course guide, the earliest PCs were equipped with an Intel CPU called the:
explanation: The earliest PCs were equipped with the Intel 8088 CPU; later generations used the 80286 ("PC/AT"), then 80386, 80486, and eventually the Pentium series.

question_text: An intelligent computer keyboard has four major divisions: Function keys, Alphanumeric keys, Numeric keys, and:
explanation: The intelligent computer keyboard has four major divisions: Function keys, Alphanumeric keys, Numeric keys, and Control keys.

question_text: To restart or reboot a computer using a specific key combination, the course guide states you should press:
option_b: Alt, Ctrl and Del keys simultaneously
explanation: The course guide notes that to restart or reboot a computer, one presses the Alt, Ctrl and Del keys simultaneously.

option_c: Using a laser beam to fuse toner to paper

question_text: VGA and SVGA, common monitor display standards, mainly differ in terms of:
option_b: Resolution, the number of dots (pixels) the monitor can display in each direction
option_c: The physical size of the monitor only
option_d: The type of power cable used
explanation: VGA (640x480) and SVGA (800x600) refer to the monitor's resolution, meaning how many pixels it can display in each direction; more pixels generally means better image quality.

question_text: Flatbed scanners are best suited for a wide variety of scanning needs, but are a poor choice for:
option_a: Scanning pages from a book without damaging the original
option_b: Scanning multi-page text documents quickly, since only one page can be scanned at a time
option_c: Scanning objects of different shapes and sizes
explanation: Flatbed scanners are versatile for varied shapes and sizes, including book pages, but scanning multi-page documents is slow and tedious since only one page can be scanned at a time.

question_text: The Uninterruptible Power Supply System (UPS) is capable of all of the following EXCEPT:
option_a: Converting the public electricity raw line into a conditioned, fine line
option_b: Storing electrical energy when the public electricity line is live
option_c: Releasing stored electrical energy to the computer when the public electricity line is dead
option_d: Permanently increasing a computer's processing speed
explanation: The UPS conditions incoming voltage, stores electrical energy while power is live, and releases that stored energy when power goes out; it has no effect on a computer's processing speed.

question_text: A line voltage transformer is a device meant to:
option_b: Step up or step down a voltage as needed, such as converting 240V to 110V
option_c: Replace the need for a keyboard
explanation: A voltage transformer steps up or steps down voltage as needed; for example, in Nigeria a 110V computer requires a transformer to step down the local 240V supply.

question_text: Air conditioners are needed in a computing environment mainly to condition the temperature and to:
option_a: Prevent dust, since dust is metallic in nature and can bridge electronic circuits
option_c: Increase the volume of speaker output
explanation: Air conditioners are needed to condition temperature and prevent dust, which is metallic in nature and, if allowed to settle on circuits, can bridge two circuits and cause serious damage.
